title: Saved By "The Outages"
summary:
Saved By "The Outages" 

             
             
            Ever since the FAA ground stop and Microsoft outage at the end of last week, markets have been on high alert for additional tech-related outages. Whether it's due to that vigilance or an actual uptick in underlying problems, today's news cycle was happy to oblige the concern. The most notable development was a data system outage at the NSA. Separately, there were other outages reported by Apple and Microsoft. There was also an alert put out by the FBI regarding AI-related exploit vulnerability. All of the above (but mostly the NSA stuff) caused stocks to swoon. Bonds benefited from a very modest flight to safety which helped Treasuries and MBS turn green around 10:30am ET. After that, trading was fairly uneventful into the close.

title: Mortgage Rates Move Modestly Lower
summary: Mortgage rates endured a reasonably sharp losing streak heading into this week. While yesterday's increase was barely detectable, it was still technically another day in that streak.   Things are different today. Once again, the movement wasn't extreme, but this time around, it played out in a more friendly direction. Average top tier 30yr fixed rates fell 0.03% to 7.48% for top tier scenarios.  This wasn't destined to be the case earlier in the day. Rates started out fairly flat and some lenders were even slightly higher. Then news broke regarding an outage for a communication system inside the NSA. This was troubling enough to financial markets that stocks swooned and bonds improved. Any time bonds change enough during the trading day, mortgage lenders are more and more likely to make rate adjustments.

title: Asset, Audit Tools; FICO's 1/1 Deadline... What Every Lender Should Know; Two-Edged Tech Sword... Apple's Doing What?
summary: “Rob, we’re about to have a come apart down here. Too many failures of systems in the last few days, and now the large banks (Chase, Wells, Truist, and others) were hit with an outage. Artificial intelligence and tech problems are not only impacting my lender clients, and my company, but also the overall financial system.” Yup, its impact is widespread. title: Strong Retail Sales Only a Mild Inconvenience For Bonds
summary: Don't bet against the U.S. consumer, apparently. Retail sales may have merely hit the 0.2% forecast at the headline level, but the "control group" (think "core retail sales") came in at 0.6% vs 0.4% and the previous month was revised up from 0.1% to 0.5%. These are strong numbers, even after accounting for inflation. Bonds were slightly stronger before the data came out and 10yr yields moved 2bps higher immediately following the data, but that's been the extent of the damage so far. Any additional volatility will have to find different motivations. On that note, NVDA reports earnings after the bell (4pm ET or shortly thereafter) and the potential implications for equities go without saying. That said, bond yields have remained higher and flatter even as stocks have moved back toward recent lows of the past 3 trading days.

title: Builder Rate Incentives Give New-Home Buyers a 114-Basis-Point Edge
summary: Homebuilders are gaining a financing advantage over existing-home sellers, offering mortgage rates more than a full percentage point below those secured by resale buyers, according to new research from Realtor.com.The average starting mortgage rate for new-home buyers was 5.01% in the third quarter, compared with 6.15% for existing-home buyers, a 114-basis-point difference. On a $400,000 purchase with 10% down, that translates to approximately $258 less in monthly interest during the first year, Realtor.com reported Tuesday.
